tripline.name: tripline
tripline.title: tripline: a CI gate for detection rules | Sami Ali
tripline.desc: tripline replays recorded ATT&CK telemetry through Sigma rules on every pull request. The stock SigmaHQ setuid rule matched 0 of 36 events; a replacement rule matches 2.
tripline.fact: A CI gate that replays recorded ATT&CK telemetry through Sigma rules and fails the pull request when an expected rule stops firing. 14 scenarios, 10 passing, 4 pending (Windows); 186 tests.
tripline.found_title: The stock setuid rule matched nothing
tripline.left_title: A replacement rule matches the two chmod runs

reading.unit: events matched by the stock rule
reading.caption: The stock SigmaHQ Setuid and Setgid rule matched 0 of 36 events in telemetry recorded from Atomic Red Team's T1548.001 tests on a GitHub-hosted Linux runner. The replacement rule matches 2.

home.found: 0 of 36 events matched by the stock rule
home.tolerance: One recording per scenario, no benign corpus; 4 Windows scenarios pending

sinkline.name: sinkline
sinkline.title: sinkline: taint analysis for Python web apps | Sami Ali
sinkline.desc: sinkline follows request data across functions and files to dangerous sinks. 91 tests; F1 0.992 on a 109-line self-labeled benchmark, Bandit 0.579.
sinkline.fact: A static analyzer that follows request data across functions and files and reports it only when it reaches a dangerous sink without a sanitizer for that bug class. 91 tests; 109-line self-labeled benchmark.
sinkline.found_title: A shell injection in its own Action, and the benchmark misses
sinkline.left_title: The reading against Bandit on the same lines

record.reference: Bandit 1.9.4 on the same 109 labeled lines (bench/corpus, labeled by the author)

reading.caption: Precision 1.000, recall 0.984, F1 0.992 on sinkline's own 109-line benchmark, which is small and labeled by its author. Bandit 1.9.4 scores F1 0.579 on the same lines.

main.note: Ticks are grouped by outcome, not in file order.

home.tolerance: Small benchmark labeled by its author

kevgate.name: kevgate
kevgate.title: kevgate: KEV-ranked vulnerability intake | Sami Ali
kevgate.desc: kevgate ranks scanner findings by CISA KEV, EPSS, CVSS and asset criticality. Six surviving mutants killed, 277 tests, and CI that tests NetworkPolicy and Pod Security on kind.
kevgate.fact: A small API that turns scanner findings into a remediation queue ranked by CISA KEV, EPSS, CVSS and asset criticality, shipped with a container, Helm chart, Terraform and a CI security pipeline. 277 tests on main.
kevgate.found_title: Six defects survived the test suite
kevgate.left_title: Six mutants killed, and controls tested in CI

record.reference: its own controls (authentication, rate limits, NetworkPolicy, Pod Security) and a list of six mutants, tested in a kind cluster in CI

reading.caption: Six defects had survived the test suite; tests added in 0.1.1 now fail when each one is reintroduced. The suite went from 227 to 277 tests.

home.against: Its own six surviving mutants; kind cluster in CI
home.tolerance: Demonstration scope: one replica, SQLite, LocalStack only

kevgate-admit.name: kevgate-admit
kevgate-admit.title: kevgate-admit: Kubernetes admission webhook | Sami Ali
kevgate-admit.desc: kevgate-admit is a Go admission webhook that denies or warns on workloads whose image digests carry KEV-listed or over-threshold vulnerabilities. 72 tests, 95% coverage, kind end-to-end run in CI.
kevgate-admit.fact: An admission webhook that denies or warns on workloads whose image digests carry KEV-listed or over-threshold vulnerabilities. 72 tests, 95% coverage, and a kind end-to-end run in CI. It does not scan images itself.
kevgate-admit.found_title: What the webhook was checked against
kevgate-admit.left_title: Five outcomes on kind, and coverage

fuzzdiff.name: fuzzdiff
fuzzdiff.title: fuzzdiff: picohttpparser in safe Rust | Sami Ali
fuzzdiff.desc: fuzzdiff ports the picohttpparser HTTP parser from C to safe Rust and checks it against the original with differential tests, property tests, seeded bugs and libFuzzer smoke runs.
fuzzdiff.fact: picohttpparser ported from C to safe Rust and checked against the original with differential tests, seeded bugs and libFuzzer. 29 tests, 95.88% line coverage; Rust is about 1.4x to 1.5x slower on head parsing. No vulnerability found.
fuzzdiff.found_title: A harness exception that would have hidden a bug
fuzzdiff.left_title: Three seeded bugs caught, and a clean control

kev-risk-prioritization.name: kev-risk-prioritization
kev-risk-prioritization.title: kev-risk-prioritization | Sami Ali
kev-risk-prioritization.desc: A small standard-library script that ranks scan findings with KEV status first, run on a 20-finding synthetic sample: 12 of 12 top slots are KEV findings, against 9 for a CVSS-only sort.
kev-risk-prioritization.fact: The scoring idea behind kevgate as a standard-library script, run on a 20-finding synthetic sample. Synthetic data only. 9 tests.
kev-risk-prioritization.found_title: A CVSS-only sort leaves KEV findings out of the top 12
kev-risk-prioritization.left_title: The risk score puts all 12 KEV findings first

reading.unit: top slots held by KEV findings
reading.caption: On a synthetic 20-finding sample the risk score puts all 12 KEV findings in its top 12. A CVSS-only sort of the same findings puts 9 there.

failed_first.text: The stock SigmaHQ Setuid and Setgid rule matched 0 of 36 recorded events. A replacement rule matches the 2 chmod executions.
4 of the 7 Windows scenarios have no accepted recording yet and count as zero in the 68% weighted coverage.
The GitHub Action put its inputs into a shell line, a script-injection flaw in its own code. Fixed in 0.4.1.
Six defects survived 227 tests, including a non-constant-time key comparison. 0.1.1 adds tests that kill all six.
The harness treated any folded-header error in strict mode as the documented deviation, which would have hidden a real bug. The exception is now narrowed.
